macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stock futures and global markets rebound as oil retreats
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures edged higher as oil prices eased and investors assessed renewed U.S.-Iran tensions after fresh strikes reignited geopolitical anxiety. Reuters also reported that European shares rose in choppy trading and Asian markets climbed, though gains were capped by oil-driven inflation concerns.

items.title: Wall Street closes higher as chip stocks offset Iran worries
items.summary: U.S. stocks ended higher, with the S&P 500 up 0.81% and the Nasdaq 100 up 1.62%, as a surge in chip shares outweighed geopolitical concerns tied to the Iran conflict. MarketScreener also noted that semiconductor weakness had been a theme during the session before the late rebound.

items.title: Treasury yields steady while investors await domestic data amid Iran flare-up
items.summary: U.S. Treasury yields were mostly steady after a prior spike, as traders focused on incoming U.S. economic data and the impact of heightened Middle East tensions. The moves reflected a broader wait-and-see stance in fixed income markets.

items.title: Reuters: Micron plans more than $250 billion of U.S. investment through 2035
items.summary: Micron Technology said it will invest more than $250 billion in the U.S. through 2035, citing surging AI-driven memory-chip demand and Washington’s push for domestic semiconductor production. The announcement is one of the largest long-term manufacturing commitments in the sector.

items.title: Reuters: Semiconductor stocks wobble after Iran tensions and Samsung signals
items.summary: Reuters reported that U.S. semiconductor shares were under pressure after renewed U.S.-Iran tensions and disappointing signals from Samsung Electronics rattled confidence in the AI trade. The sector’s recent volatility has become a major market theme.

items.title: U.S. economy slows more than expected in second quarter
items.summary: The Commerce Department reported that U.S. GDP grew at a 1.5% annualized pace in the second quarter, below expectations and slower than the prior quarter. PBS NewsHour said the slowdown came as markets digested the Fed’s decision to keep rates unchanged despite three dissents favoring a hike.

items.title: Federal Reserve leaves rates unchanged despite three dissents
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged, but the decision drew three dissents, all arguing for a rate increase. The split underscores continued pressure on policymakers from elevated inflation and resilient labor-market conditions.

items.title: IMF cuts 2026 global growth forecast, citing Iran war fallout
items.summary: The IMF lowered its 2026 world growth forecast to 3.0%, saying AI-related demand is partly offsetting the drag from the energy shock tied to the Iran war. The revision highlights how geopolitical risks are feeding into the macro outlook.

items.title: China producer inflation accelerates to near four-year high
items.summary: Reuters said China’s producer price inflation rose for a fourth straight month and reached its highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also increased. The data point to persistent cost pressures for manufacturers.

items.title: Japan wholesale prices jump on higher energy costs and weak yen
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that Japan’s wholesale prices spiked in July, reflecting higher energy costs and a weak yen. The move adds to inflation concerns and supports expectations that the Bank of Japan may keep normalizing policy.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major cryptocurrencies rebounded above $64K amid macro-driven risk appetite
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $64,000 and briefly pushed above $65,000 as easing oil prices and stronger equity sentiment improved risk appetite; BTC rose about 2.16% in one market snapshot, while Ethereum, XRP, Solana, and Dogecoin also gained. Market data cited in coverage showed roughly $200 million to $330 million in liquidations over the last 24 hours, reflecting a sharp swing in leveraged positioning.

items.title: Hong Kong tightens crypto-platform security rules
items.summary: Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission moved to require crypto platforms to abandon SMS authentication, signaling a stricter approach to exchange security and operational controls. The change adds to a broader regulatory push in the region as exchanges adapt compliance systems.

items.title: Bank of Korea defends its bank-first stablecoin policy
items.summary: South Korea’s central bank reiterated support for a bank-led stablecoin framework even as legislative deadlock continues, underscoring tensions between innovation goals and financial-stability concerns. The policy debate remains one of the most closely watched regulatory stories in Asian crypto markets.

items.title: U.S. CLARITY Act vote drives Coinbase legal leadership change
items.summary: Coinbase’s top legal executive, Paul Grewal, exited ahead of a crucial CLARITY vote, highlighting how U.S. crypto policy uncertainty is shaping corporate strategy. The timing points to ongoing regulatory pressure around market-structure legislation in Washington.

items.title: XRP gains as SWIFT-linked banking payments story expands
items.summary: XRP advanced after reporting tied SWIFT to Ripple-linked banks for blockchain payments, reinforcing investor focus on real-world settlement use cases. The move came alongside broader gains in major crypto assets.

items.title: BlackRock reportedly moved large BTC and ETH holdings to Coinbase
items.summary: Onchain monitoring reported that BlackRock deposited 2,700 BTC and 52,956 ETH, worth roughly $256.8 million combined, to Coinbase. The transfers drew attention because large institutional flows can influence short-term market liquidity and sentiment.

items.title: Bitdeer unveils $36 million Nevada Bitcoin-mining factory
items.summary: Bitdeer said it is building a $36 million factory in Nevada, a notable expansion in Bitcoin mining infrastructure. The project adds to a wave of capital spending by miners positioning for lower-cost hardware and regional capacity growth.

items.title: PayPal expands PYUSD stablecoin onto Polygon
items.summary: PayPal brought its PYUSD stablecoin to Polygon’s Open Money Stack, extending the stablecoin’s reach into a major Ethereum scaling ecosystem. The move is a meaningful product development for blockchain payments and stablecoin utility.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: AWS growth accelerates as Amazon boosts tech spending
items.summary: Amazon said AWS revenue rose 37% in the April-June quarter, its fastest pace in 18 quarters, and it plans to increase spending on AI and other technology by more than $20 billion. The move signals a major near-term expansion in cloud and infrastructure investment.

items.title: Meta launches new model API and cheaper pricing push
items.summary: Techmeme reported that Meta launched a Meta Model API and described pricing as about 25% of the cost of competing OpenAI and Anthropic offerings. The company is positioning price as a key competitive advantage in its developer platform strategy.

items.title: Meta opens Muse Spark 1.1 to U.S. developers
items.summary: Meta released Muse Spark 1.1, which Techmeme says is capable of more advanced coding and represents a step-change from the first generation. The model is being made available in a public API preview for U.S. developers.

items.title: Meta announces first data center in Canada
items.summary: Meta said it will build its first data center in Canada, a 1GW facility in Alberta expected to cost about $9 billion and take two to three years to construct. Techmeme says it will be Meta’s 33rd data center overall.

items.title: Micron expands U.S. capital spending commitment to $250 billion
items.summary: Techmeme reported that Micron raised its U.S. capex commitment to $250 billion through 2035, adding $50 billion for projects in New York, Idaho, Virginia, and elsewhere. The company also plans a $500 million investment in GlobalWafers.

items.title: Swift launches blockchain-based shared ledger
items.summary: Reuters reported that Swift launched a blockchain-based shared ledger with 16 banks, including Citi and HSBC, to support round-the-clock payments. The initiative is also aimed at competing with the stablecoin sector.

items.title: India removes import duties on some mobile phone and electronics parts
items.summary: Reuters said India scrapped import duties on certain components used to make mobile phones and other electronic devices, eliminating 7.5% and 5% levies. The policy could benefit manufacturers such as Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: Apple and Broadcom expand chip-supply deal
items.summary: Reuters reported that Apple plans to spend more than $30 billion under a chip-supply agreement with Broadcom, which will also expand a factory in Colorado. The deal underscores Apple’s continued investment in U.S.-based semiconductor supply.

items.title: EU lawmakers advance child-abuse scanning proposal for tech platforms
items.summary: Reuters reported that EU lawmakers backed reinstating temporary rules that would allow Google, Meta, and other platforms to detect and remove child sexual abuse material. The proposal revives a previously rejected measure.

items.title: Block reaches $45 million settlement over Cash App fraud claims
items.summary: Techmeme’s River feed reported that Block agreed to pay $45 million and offer live customer support for Cash App to settle claims from 46 U.S. states over alleged fraud protection failures. The settlement is a significant regulatory and consumer-protection development for digital payments.
